advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Publish gate_scratch_volume_in_service=-1 on the tick even when scratch_volume_id is empty/unresolved, per AC6's 'never go silent' heartbeat contract.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:391: scratch_volume_id="${GATE_SCRATCH_VOLUME_ID:-$(head -n 1 "$GATE_SCRATCH_VOLUME_ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)}"
infra/scripts/observability.sh:396: if [ -n "$scratch_volume_id" ]; then
Ticket eb65 AC6 / plan-review checklist: 'gate_scratch_volume_in_service must publish a value on EVERY recurring observability tick — emitting -1 ... never going silent'
The sibling gate_scratch_mounted heartbeat publishes unconditionally on every tick (observability.sh:383-384), whereas this metric is conditional on a non-empty id.
advisory.finding: When the gate-scratch volume-id cannot be resolved (GATE_SCRATCH_VOLUME_ID unset AND the id file missing/empty), the whole heartbeat block is skipped and NO gate_scratch_volume_in_service datapoint is published — the publisher goes silent instead of emitting -1, contradicting the ticket's AC6 heartbeat contract ('must publish a value on EVERY recurring tick ... emitting -1 ... never going silent').
scenarios: Host provisioned before this change (no id file) or user_data's printf produced an empty line because the gate_scratch_volume_id template var was empty.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/guard that the host id file must track aws_ebs_volume.gate_scratch.id across volume replacement, or key the alarm dimension off the same host-derived id, so publisher and alarm cannot silently reference different VolumeIds.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:411: --dimensions InstanceId="$IID",VolumeId="$scratch_volume_id",mount="$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT"
infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf: dimensions { ... VolumeId = aws_ebs_volume.gate_scratch.id ... }
infra/terraform/user_data.sh:239: printf '%s\n' "${gate_scratch_volume_id}" >"$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/../gate-scratch-volume-id" (written only at first boot cloud-init)
advisory.finding: The published metric's VolumeId dimension is the id read from the host-written id file ($scratch_volume_id), while the alarm's VolumeId dimension is aws_ebs_volume.gate_scratch.id from Terraform state; these are the same source only at first boot, so a later volume replacement (user_data runs once) leaves the publisher emitting under the OLD id and the alarm watching the NEW id.
scenarios: The gate-scratch EBS volume is replaced (new id) without an instance re-launch that re-runs first-boot cloud-init, so the on-disk id file keeps the old id.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure gate_scratch_volume_in_service is published on every tick (a definite -1 when the volume id is unknown) OR provision the volume-id file on existing hosts, so treat_missing_data="breaching" does not page healthy pre-change instances.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:396: `if [ -n "$scratch_volume_id" ]; then` — the entire put-metric-data block is gated on a non-empty volume id
infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:473: `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` combined with datapoints_to_alarm=6/evaluation_periods=6 means sustained absence of datapoints breaches

infra/terraform/user_data.sh:239: `printf '%s\n' "${gate_scratch_volume_id}" >"$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/../gate-scratch-volume-id"` — the file is only created at provisioning time, so already-running hosts have no source for scratch_volume_id
advisory.finding: The gate_scratch_volume_not_in_service alarm uses treat_missing_data="breaching", but observability.sh only publishes gate_scratch_volume_in_service when $scratch_volume_id is non-empty; a host whose volume-id file is missing (e.g. any instance provisioned before this user_data.sh change, since user_data only runs at (re)provision) never emits the metric and will page spuriously even when the scratch volume is fully mounted and healthy.
scenarios: An existing production host is not reprovisioned after this deploy: the volume-id file is absent, the metric is never published, and rebar-gate-scratch-volume-not-in-service pages within 30 minutes despite a healthy mounted volume.
advisory.suggested_fix: In observability.sh, publish the metric unconditionally: when $scratch_volume_id is empty, publish value -1 (unknown) with the known VolumeId dimension omitted or a sentinel, instead of skipping put-metric-data entirely; alternatively backfill the volume-id file on existing hosts.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Set an explicit mode on the gate-scratch-volume-id file (or document why the ambient umask is acceptable) to match the recorded chmod-first marker discipline.
evidence: infra/terraform/user_data.sh:230-235: comment documents chmod FIRST then populate as the recorded intent (bug ad8d-4274-ef43-4f44 F4)
infra/terraform/user_data.sh:239: `printf '%s\n' "${gate_scratch_volume_id}" >"$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/../gate-scratch-volume-id"` writes to the ROOT parent dir with no explicit mode
advisory.finding: The gate-scratch-volume-id marker file is written with the ambient umask (no chmod), whereas the adjacent .gate-scratch-required/.gate-scratch-mounted markers are deliberately created after a chmod-first ordering; the new write breaks the "tighten, then populate" ordering that the surrounding comment records as load-bearing.
scenarios: The volume-id file lands world-readable under the ambient umask on the root filesystem.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add unit tests for main(['--metric-value', ...]) covering the missing-arg exit code 2 and the --host-report metric-value output (1/0/-1).
evidence: scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py:285-287: `if not args.volume_id or not args.mount: print(...); return 2`
Named violating input: `main(['--metric-value'])` must return 2; no test asserts this exit code or message.
ABSENCE: search for `metric-value` finds only source references (observability.sh and the script itself), no test invocation.
advisory.finding: The new --metric-value CLI branch (argument validation and host-report vs lsblk resolution) added to main() is not covered by the dedicated unit test file. The error path returning 2 when --volume-id/--mount are missing is untested.
scenarios: A regression in the argument validation (e.g. defaulting to plan-mode) would go undetected.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that sets GATE_SCRATCH_VOLUME_ID_FILE with the scratch volume mounted at the expected mount and asserts gate_scratch_volume_in_service publishes [1].
evidence: scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py:188: `return METRIC_IN_SERVICE if mount == expected_mount else METRIC_NOT_IN_SERVICE`
infra/scripts/observability.sh:403: `case "$scratch_volume_value" in` with branch `1) scratch_volume_value="1" ;;`

Named violating input: a host report where the scratch volume vol-06780b8557d1416b7 IS mounted at the expected mount (`SERIAL="vol06780b8557d1416b7" MOUNTPOINT="/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch"`) with GATE_SCRATCH_VOLUME_ID_FILE set must publish [1]; no test asserts this. If the function/shell regressed to never emit 1 the alarm would page permanently and no test would catch it.
ABSENCE: only test_scratch_volume_join_failure_publishes_unknown_every_tick (value -1) sets GATE_SCRATCH_VOLUME_ID_FILE; the mounted heartbeat test at line 351 does not.
blocking.finding: The healthy heartbeat value '1' (in-service) — the exact value the new alarm keys on (threshold=1, LessThanThreshold) — is exercised by no test. volume_in_service_metric_value's METRIC_IN_SERVICE branch and the shell publish path for value=1 are both untested; test_a_mounted_scratch_volume_publishes_the_heartbeat_and_its_usage never sets GATE_SCRATCH_VOLUME_ID_FILE, so scratch_volume_id is empty and the entire new block at observability.sh:396 is skipped.
scenarios: A regression that makes the healthy path publish 0 or -1 instead of 1 would cause the new alarm to page constantly, undetected by the suite.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests asserting volume_in_service_metric_value returns 0 when the volume is present in the host report but mounted at a different (or empty) mount, and that the shell publishes [0] end-to-end.
evidence: scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py:188: `return METRIC_IN_SERVICE if mount == expected_mount else METRIC_NOT_IN_SERVICE`

Named violating input: `volume_in_service_metric_value('vol-06780b8557d1416b7', '/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch', 'NAME="nvme2n1" SERIAL="vol06780b8557d1416b7" MOUNTPOINT=""')` must return 0 (present but not at expected mount); no test asserts this.
ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_assert_volumes_in_service_dcc3.py was not updated in this diff and imports do not include volume_in_service_metric_value; the only new metric test (line 336) covers -1 only.
blocking.finding: The NOT-IN-SERVICE value '0' (volume present in host report but mounted elsewhere / unmounted) — the actual production bug this feature exists to monitor — is untested at both the Python function level and the shell publish level.
scenarios: The delivered-but-not-in-effect state (volume attached but mounted at wrong path or not mounted while device visible) would publish the wrong value and the alarm would read healthy.
